title: Hold a plastic pipe still with one hand while the other tightens its union nut snug, stopping before the thread strips
instruction: Hold the pipe still with one hand and with the other tighten the union nut on its end until it is snug against the collar, without forcing it further, then let go with both hands.
context: Plumbers and maintenance workers tighten plastic pipe fittings by hand until snug and then stop: plastic threads strip or crack when forced, and a ruined fitting leaks. Stopping at the right moment matters as much as turning. A loose pipe turns with its nut unless it is held.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A loose white plastic pipe, 150 g, 1.6 cm across and 24 cm long, along the left-right line 30 cm forward, from 9 cm right of the centre line to 15 cm left, its axis 11 cm above the table. It lies in two fixed, smooth dark supports, 2 cm right and 13 cm left of the centre line, in which it turns freely. Its right end is threaded for 2 cm, with a grey collar 2.6 cm across just past the thread. (2) A loose white plastic union nut, 20 g, 2 cm across and 1.6 cm long, with six ribs, started on the pipe's thread, its inner face 6 mm from the collar (a turn and a half short of snug). The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. Turns: the nut's net turns tightening it on the pipe since the start (each draws it 4 mm along); 1.5 brings it against the collar. Snug: at least 1.4 turns. Stripped: 2 turns or more at any time (half a turn past snug): the thread strips, the nut spins loose, and the trial scores 0. Let go: both grippers' fingertip centres (TCPs) at least 3 cm from the pipe and the nut. 1.0: snug and both let go; 0.5: at least 1 turn; 0.25: at least a quarter turn; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held with the pipe and the nut still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Turn the nut back to a turn and a half short of snug (or fit a new nut if the thread was stripped) and lay the pipe back in its supports as in the screenshot.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: PhysX has no screw thread: a joint keeps the nut on the pipe's axis and drags as they turn against each other (0.3 N m s/rad, 0.8 once snug), and the task file draws the nut 4 mm along per turn. Stripping is counted in turns past snug, not torque; the nut and the pipe do not collide. The supports are fixed and smooth. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
